Capable of being exercised only through the courts
Recognized by custom but not written into law
days.r: French inaliénable: in- + alienable
days.s: An inalienable right is a right that cannot be given away nor taken away.

days.d: An elaborate analytical or explanatory essay or discussion
f: A brief witty saying or epigram
A sudden break from the main thread of a story
A playful imitation of another writer’s style
days.r: Latin disquīsītiō “inquiry, investigation”, from disquīrō “to investigate”
days.s: Everett’s novels make abundant use of language games, conceits and disquisitions.

days.d: Unequivocally detestable
f: Mildly tedious
Strangely satisfying
Strongly scented
days.r: Latin odiōsus, from odium “hate”
days.s: Scrubbing the toilets in the bar at the end of a Saturday night is an odious task.

days.d: A large metal or pottery vessel with a handle and spout; used to hold alcoholic beverages (usually wine)
f: A small wooden cask with a tap and bung; used to store salted fish (usually herring)
A shallow silver dish with two handles; used to serve sweetmeats (usually at feasts)
A large leather bag with a stopper and strap; used to carry water (usually by travellers)
days.r: Old French flacon “flask”, from Late Latin flascō “bottle”
days.s: "He's got a venison pastry and a flagon of sack in that cupboard behind him."

days.d: Without limits in extent or size or quantity
f: Without light in depth or colour or shade
Without sound or motion or any sign of life
Without warmth in air or water or stone
days.r: Il- + limitable
days.s: The endless voyage beyond planet and galaxy into the illimitable dark.

days.d: A natural disposition to fight
f: A natural disposition to boast
A natural disposition to secrecy
A natural disposition to sulk
days.r: Bellicose + -osity
days.s: Before this news North Korea was all bellicosity and bluster.

days.d: A minor parish official who serves a ceremonial function
f: A senior parish priest who serves several churches
A village schoolmaster who teaches the poor
A country squire who owns the village lands
days.r: Old English bydel “warrant officer, herald”: bid + -le
days.s: He was a Beadle; I was a woman.

days.d: A figure consisting of three stylized human arms or legs (or three bent lines) radiating from a center
f: A figure consisting of three interlocking rings (or three overlapping circles) sharing a common center
A figure consisting of four arms bent at right angles (or four hooked lines) radiating from a center
A figure consisting of a single line wound in a spiral (or a coil) around a fixed center
days.r: French triskèle (1835); attested in English circa 1885
days.s: Both materials have the triskele geometry.
